item.text:
**4B.2 Research Note**
Bottom line: the 2024 record is mostly negative. Erdoğan did not fully entrench himself by canceling elections, but the strongest available evidence points to an unlevel playing field: tight media control, biased public broadcasting, selective repression of critics, and post-election removal of opposition winners.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | [Turkey's resurgent opposition thumps Erdogan in pivotal local elections](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkeys-resurgent-opposition-thumps-erdogan-pivotal-local-elections-2024-03-31/) | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkeys-resurgent-opposition-thumps-erdogan-pivotal-local-elections-2024-03-31/ | Opposition wins in Istanbul, Ankara, and nationwide in the March 2024 local vote show power was still electorally contestable, even if not on a level field. This is evidence against total electoral closure, but not proof of sincere restraint. | 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Mixed / Negative | [Turkey](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report says Erdoğan entered the term with continued tight media control, while TRT and other outlets favored incumbents. It also says the March 2024 local election was the ruling party’s biggest defeat since 2002, which helps show contestability but also underscores the prior informational tilt. | 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Negative | [Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says state-run media heavily favored the AKP, speech and media were restricted during the campaign and after the earthquake, and authorities threatened social media access and fined broadcasters. That is direct evidence of using media and state pressure to entrench incumbency. | 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Negative | [Turkish police detain 217 May Day protesters in Istanbul, minister says](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkish-police-fire-tear-gas-stop-may-day-protesters-reaching-istanbuls-taksim-square-2024-05-01/) | Reuters | 2024-05-02 | https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkish-police-fire-tear-gas-stop-may-day-protesters-reaching-istanbuls-taksim-square-2024-05-01/ | Erdoğan said May Day protests would not be allowed at Taksim Square; police used tear gas and rubber bullets and detained 217 people. This is evidence of security forces being used to suppress dissent and public assembly around a politically sensitive moment. | 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | [Turkey removes two more pro-Kurdish mayors from office for links to banned group](https://apnews.com/article/3c6c33fd7fa2d86c9dc34089e6a98c9b) | Associated Press | 2024-11-22 | https://apnews.com/article/3c6c33fd7fa2d86c9dc34089e6a98c9b | Elected mayors were removed and replaced with state appointees after March 2024 local-election wins, with critics calling the moves politically motivated. That is strong post-election retaliation against opposition local power. | 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Negative | [Türkiye: Government Removes Elected Opposition Mayors](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-11-07 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors | HRW says removing elected mayors, dissolving councils, and replacing them with appointees violates free and fair elections and follows a pattern of using terrorism allegations to neutralize opposition victories. | 4B.2, 4B.1 |

**Search gap**
I did not find a reliable 2024 source in this pass showing a fresh 2024 rewrite of electoral law or a clear, documented takeover of the election commission itself. The case is instead built on strong structural evidence: biased media, unequal state access, protest suppression, and after-the-fact removal of opposition winners.
